title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 106
paragraphs: After this Cyaxares died, having reigned forty years, including those years during which the Scythians had ruled, and Astyages, son of Cyaxares, received the kingdom from him. To him was born a daughter whom he named Mandane; and in his sleep it seemed to him that there passed from her so much water as to fill his city and even to flood the whole of Asia. This dream he handed over to the Magian interpreters of dreams, and when he heard from them the truth of each detail, he became afraid. And afterwards, when this Mandane was of an age to have a husband, he did not give her in marriage to any of the Medes who were his peers, because he feared the vision; but he gave her to a Persian named Cambyses, whom he found to be of good descent and of a quiet disposition, counting him in station much below a Mede of middle rank.
